players.product: Custom data-center AI silicon (new entrant; hyperscaler custom-ASIC engagement)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Akash Palkhiwala on fiscal Q3 segments: QTL revenues of $1.3 billion at an EBT margin of 69%, in line with expectations; QCT revenues of $8.5 billion at the high end of guidance with a 26% EBT margin, in line with guidance; QCT IoT revenues of $1.8 billion, up 9% versus the prior year on growth in industrial, networking and robotics products; QCT Automotive another record quarter at $1.6 billion, up 61% year over year, 'driven by accelerating demand and increasing compute content per vehicle'.
quarterly_data.figure: QTL $1.3 billion (69% EBT); QCT $8.5 billion (26% EBT); IoT $1.8 billion, +9%; Automotive $1.6 billion, +61%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Akash Palkhiwala's fiscal Q4 guidance beyond the revenue range: non-GAAP EPS of $2.05 to $2.25; QTL EBT margin of 68% to 72%, reflecting normal seasonal trends; QCT EBT margins of 23% to 25%; QCT handset revenues of approximately $5.2 billion, with sequential growth in Android offset by lower Apple product revenues; QCT IoT approximately flat versus the year-ago period, with double-digit growth in industrial, networking and robotics offset primarily by the impact of memory constraints on tablets and other consumer products; QCT Automotive another record quarter with approximately 60% year-over-year revenue growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 EPS $2.05 to $2.25; QCT EBT 23% to 25%; handsets ~$5.2 billion; Automotive ~60% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Akash Palkhiwala on the December quarter (qualitative, not formal guidance): Android is expected to grow and significantly offset the reduction in Apple, with data-center revenue starting to ramp in the first fiscal quarter, so QCT revenue in the December quarter is expected to be 'slightly up on a sequential basis'; with Apple's strong December quarter no longer in the model, 'We actually expect revenues to grow when we go from the December to the March quarter now.' He added that, with share materially less than 20%, revenue 'in 2027 from Apple product, would be less than the previous guidance we had given, which was a little over $2 billion'.
quarterly_data.figure: December-quarter QCT revenue slightly up sequentially; 2027 Apple product revenue below the prior guidance of a little over $2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cristiano Amon: this quarter Qualcomm signed a 'landmark expanded agreement with BMW', winning a highly competitive selection process to become the lead compute silicon provider for BMW's next-generation ADAS as well as Digital Cockpit. The agreement 'represents a material expansion of our automotive pipeline' and establishes Qualcomm as BMW's lead compute silicon partner 'extending across model programs well into the next decade'.

CEO Cristiano Amon on automotive: the recently announced collaboration with Stellantis supports the automotive pipeline 'well into the 2030s', and customers are shifting from socket-by-socket design awards to multi-generation strategic engagements. The fifth-generation Snapdragon Digital Chassis ramps in September with a significant increase in content per vehicle, and Qualcomm says it is on track to become the number 1 automotive semiconductor player by revenue (company claim). Raised outlook: annualized automotive sales of approximately $7 billion exiting fiscal 2026, up from the $6 billion run-rate target given last quarter. Amon: OEMs choosing next-generation silicon is 'actually increasing the automotive revenue even ahead of our expectations'. The updated fiscal 2029 targets include more than $24 billion in revenue across automotive and IoT.
quarterly_data.figure: automotive annualized ~$7 billion exiting fiscal 2026 (from $6 billion); FY2029 >$24 billion across automotive and IoT

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cristiano Amon on industrial: the Investor Day fiscal 2029 projection is $8 billion in revenue for industrial networking and robotics; the industrial design-win pipeline exceeds $7 billion, with over $3.5 billion in design wins secured this fiscal year. Channel presence exceeds 38,000 customers, and with Arduino and Edge Impulse Qualcomm's reach extends to more than 30 million users.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2029 industrial networking and robotics $8 billion; design-win pipeline >$7 billion; >$3.5 billion won this fiscal year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cristiano Amon: Qualcomm's share position at Samsung remains strong, with Snapdragon powering approximately 70% of Samsung's flagship devices; as announced at Samsung Unpacked, the collaboration is expanding across the wider Galaxy ecosystem, from the latest foldable phones and Galaxy Watches to intelligent eyewear developed with Google.
quarterly_data.figure: Snapdragon in ~70% of Samsung flagship devices

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cristiano Amon on handsets and new devices: despite overall industry contraction caused by the memory environment, Qualcomm is 'seeing early signs of an agentic smartphone cycle that will grow over time', with major Chinese OEMs preparing to bring new on-device agents and orchestrators to market. In PCs, Qualcomm is growing its leading share of design wins in Chromebooks (Snapdragon with Gemini Intelligence) and is collaborating with Microsoft on Project Solara, a chip-to-cloud platform designed for agent-first enterprise devices. The Snapdragon START program gives eyewear brands a complete smart-glasses reference platform, with roughly 600 million global eyewear units shipped every year.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly 600 million eyewear units a year (Snapdragon START smart-glasses program)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cristiano Amon on whether U.S.-China restrictions affect the data-center business: 'For the engagements we have today, we're not restricted. It's within the category of other companies that are also providing solutions for China. That is not a concern at this moment.'

CFO Akash Palkhiwala on QTL: the licensing model has 'a cap on the total royalties based on the device ASP'; to the extent device prices rise below the cap, some benefit accrues to QTL, while above the cap it makes no difference to QTL revenue.
